speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is pain, what is pleasure?
premises: Pain defined as separation, pleasure as union: saṃgrahena sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ māṃ prati sthitam idaṃ śṛṇu prabho.
Saukhyam eṣa bhavatā samāgamaḥ: just to be in Thy presence is pleasure.
Svāminā viraha eva duḥkhitā: being carried away from Thy presence brings deep pain.
The verse defines pain/pleasure before proving the definition across twenty moves.
inference: Pain = separation, pleasure = union. The definition precedes the proof.
uncertainties: Whether 'sukhaduḥkhalakṣaṇaṃ' means 'definition of pleasure and pain' or 'characteristic of pleasure and pain' is unresolved.
Whether 'viraha' means 'separation' or 'absence' is unresolved.
Swamiji: ch13+14 composed 'in his senses' (saṅgraha = sane summary) vs the gone/ecstatic chapters — the definition-verse is deliberate doctrine, not effusion.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What blocks perception?
premises: Antar apy atitarām aṇīyasī yā tvadaprathanakālikāsti me: a minute impurity in the internal state, keeping me from perceiving You.
Tām apīśa parimṛjya sarvataḥ: remove that impurity completely.
Svaṃ svarūpam amalaṃ prakāśaya: reveal Your pure form.
The verse asks for removal of the subtle impurity (āṇavamala) that blocks perception.
inference: A minute impurity blocks perception; remove it completely and reveal Your pure form.
uncertainties: Whether 'aṇīyasī' means 'minute' or 'subtle' is unresolved.
Whether 'parimṛjya' means 'wiping away' or 'removing' is unresolved.
Swamiji (Hymns to Shiva ch13) reads the kālikā as the āṇavamala remnant — māyīya and kārma malas already gone, only the minute internal dirt blocking perception remains; minted as live L0 fork.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the sole longing?
premises: Tāvake vapuṣi viśvanirbhare citsudhārasamaye niratyaye: residing in Your universal body, filled with supreme nectar of consciousness.
Tiṣṭhataḥ satatam arcataḥ prabhuṃ: residing, worshipping the Lord constantly.
Jīvitaṃ mṛtam athānyad astu me: let me die, let me go to hell or heaven — I don't care, so long as I have Your worship.
The verse states the devotee's sole longing: reside in Your body and worship, indifferent to life/death.
inference: Reside in Your universal body and worship constantly; life/death indifferent — worship is the sole longing.
uncertainties: Whether 'jīvitaṃ mṛtam' means 'let me live or die' or 'whether living or dead' is unresolved.
Whether 'anyad' means 'other' or 'anything else' is unresolved.
Swamiji: jīvitam/mṛtam/anyad spans hell, heaven, even mokṣa — all indifferent against constant worship; the verse's only desire is satatam arcana.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: When is ego appropriate?
premises: Īśvaro 'ham aham eva rūpavān paṇḍito 'smi subhago 'smi ko 'paraḥ: I am Īśvara, beautiful, learned, charming — who else is parallel?
Matsamo 'sti jagatīti śobhate mānitā tvadanurāgiṇaḥ param: this ego shines beautifully only in those devoted to You.
The verse presents the devotee's ego as appropriate only when devoted to You.
inference: Ego shines beautifully only in those devoted to You: 'I am Īśvara' is appropriate only with devotion.
uncertainties: Whether 'mānitā' means 'ego' or 'pride' is unresolved.
Whether 'param' means 'supreme' or 'ultimately' is unresolved.
Swamiji: this ego (mānitā) SHINES in devotees but damns the detached ('let them go to the dogs'); maxim: he who is attached to God is beautiful because love for God is charming.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What makes worship possible?
premises: Devadeva bhavadadvayāmṛtākhyātisaṃharaṇalabdhajanmanā: O Lord of Lords, by the touch of oneness, senses nectarized.
Tad yathāsthitapadārthasaṃvidā māṃ kuruṣva caraṇārcanocitam: make me worthy of worshipping Your feet.
The verse asks for senses nectarized by oneness, so worship becomes possible.
inference: Senses nectarized by oneness: make me worthy of worshipping Your feet.
uncertainties: Whether 'labdhajanmanā' means 'born of' or 'attained through' is unresolved.
Whether 'yathāsthitapadārtha' means 'things as they stand' or 'things as they are' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is the sequence?
premises: Dhyāyate tad anu dṛśyate tataḥ spṛśyate ca parameśvaraḥ svayam: meditated, then seen, then touched — the Lord Himself.
Yatra pūjanamahotsavaḥ sa me sarvadāstu bhavato 'nubhāvataḥ: where worship-festival is, let it always be mine by Your grace.
The verse sequences meditation → vision → touch → festival.
inference: Meditation, then vision, then touch: the Lord Himself. Worship-festival always, by grace.
uncertainties: Whether 'dhyāyate' is passive or active is unresolved.
Whether 'anubhāvataḥ' means 'by grace' or 'by experience' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What grounds what?
premises: Yady athāsthitapadārthadarśanaṃ yuṣmadarcanamahotsavaś ca yaḥ: if seeing things as they stand and worship-festival —
yugmam etad itaretarāśrayaṃ bhaktiśāliṣu sadā vijṛmbhate: this pair mutually grounds, always blooms in devotees.
Seeing and worship-festival mutually ground each other in devotees.
inference: Seeing things as they stand and worship-festival mutually ground each other in devotees.
uncertainties: Whether 'yugmam' means 'pair' or 'couple' is unresolved.
Whether 'itaretarāśraya' means 'mutually grounding' or 'reciprocal support' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How is worship drunk?
premises: Tattadindriyamukhena santataṃ yuṣmadarcanarasāyanāsavam: through each sense, the worship-rasa-nectar.
Sarvabhāvacaṣakeṣu pūriteṣv āpibann api bhaveyam unmadaḥ: drinking, even, from filled cups of all things, may I be mad.
The verse asks to drink worship-rasa through every sense, becoming mad with it.
inference: Drink worship-rasa through every sense, from filled cups of all things — may I be mad with it.
uncertainties: Whether 'rasāyanāsava' means 'worship-rasa-nectar' or 'rasa-nectar of worship' is unresolved.
Whether 'unmadaḥ' means 'mad' or 'intoxicated' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is knowable?
premises: Anyavedyam aṇumātram asti na: no thing is knowable apart from You.
Svaprakāśam akhilaṃ vijṛmbhate: all shines by self-luminosity.
Yatra nātha bhavataḥ pure sthitaṃ tatra me kuru sadā tavārcituḥ: where You dwell, make me always Your worshipper.
The verse: nothing apart from You is knowable; all shines by self-luminosity; make me Your worshipper where You dwell.
inference: Nothing apart from You is knowable; all shines by self-luminosity; make me Your worshipper where You dwell.
uncertainties: Whether 'anyavedyam' means 'knowable apart' or 'known by another' is unresolved.
Whether 'pure' means 'city' or 'abode' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What makes worthy?
premises: Dāsadhāmni viniyojito 'py ahaṃ svecchayaiva parameśvara tvayā: even deployed in the slave's abode, by Your will.
Darśanena na kim asmi pātritaḥ pādasaṃvahanakarmaṇāpi vā: am I not made worthy by seeing, or even by foot-massage?
The verse: even in the slave's abode, by Your will — am I not made worthy by seeing or foot-massage?
inference: Even in the slave's abode, by Your will — am I not made worthy by seeing or foot-massage?
uncertainties: Whether 'dāsadhāmni' means 'in the slave's abode' or 'in the servant's place' is unresolved.
Whether 'pātritaḥ' means 'made worthy' or 'qualified' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Why delay?
premises: Śaktipātasamaye vicāraṇaṃ prāptam īśa na karoṣi karhicit: at the time of grace-descent, You never investigate.
Adya māṃ prati kim āgataṃ yataḥ svaprakāśanavidhau vilambase: what has come to me today that You delay in self-manifestation?
The verse: grace-descent needs no investigation; why delay self-manifestation?
inference: Grace-descent needs no investigation; why delay self-manifestation?
uncertainties: Whether 'vicāraṇaṃ' means 'investigation' or 'deliberation' is unresolved.
Whether 'vilambase' means 'delay' or 'linger' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Where is You seen?
premises: Tatra tatra viṣaye bahirvibhāty antare ca parameśvarīyutam: there and there, in things outside, shines, and inside, with Pārvatī.
Tvāṃ jagattritayanirbharaṃ sadā lokayeya nijapāṇipūjitam: may I always see You, filling the three worlds, worshipped by my own hand.
The verse: see You filling all three worlds, worshipped by my own hand.
inference: See You filling all three worlds, inside and outside with Pārvatī, worshipped by my own hand.
uncertainties: Whether 'bahirvibhāty' means 'shines outside' or 'is manifest outside' is unresolved.
Whether 'nijapāṇipūjitam' means 'worshipped by my own hand' or 'worshipped by own hand' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How to ascend?
premises: Svāmisaudham abhisandhimātrato nirvibandham adhiruhya sarvadā: ascending the Lord's abode by mere resolve, without obstacle, always.
Syāṃ prasāda paramāmṛtāsavāpānakeliparilabdhanirvṛtiḥ: may I attain the bliss of the nectar-drinking play of grace.
The verse: ascend by mere resolve; attain the bliss of grace's nectar-drinking play.
inference: Ascend by mere resolve; attain the bliss of grace's nectar-drinking play.
uncertainties: Whether 'abhisandhimātrato' means 'by mere resolve' or 'by resolve alone' is unresolved.
Whether 'prasāda' means 'grace' or 'favor' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How is worship offered?
premises: Yatsamastasubhagārthavastuṣu sparśamātravidhinā camatkṛtim: touching beautiful things, wonder (camatkāra).
Tāṃ samarpayati tena te vapuḥ pūjayanty acalabhaktiśālinaḥ: offering that wonder, the devotees worship Your body.
The verse: touching beautiful things gives wonder; offering it, devotees worship Your body.
inference: Touching beautiful things gives wonder (camatkāra); offering it, devotees worship Your body.
uncertainties: Whether 'sparśamātravidhinā' means 'by mere touch' or 'by the method of touch' is unresolved.
Whether 'camatkṛtim' means 'wonder' or 'relish' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: How does the world dance?
premises: Sphārayasy akhilam ātmanā sphuran viśvam āmṛśasi rūpam āmṛśan: You spread all by Yourself, shining; You touch the form, touching.
Yat svayaṃ nijarasena ghurṇase tat samullasati bhāvamaṇḍalam: what You whirl by Your own rasa, that world-circle dances.
The verse: You spread all by Yourself; the world dances by Your rasa.
inference: You spread all by Yourself; the world dances by Your rasa.
uncertainties: Whether 'sphārayasy' means 'You spread' or 'You extend' is unresolved.
Whether 'ghurṇase' means 'You whirl' or 'You stir' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: Where is fear?
premises: Yo 'vikalpam idam arthamaṇḍalaṃ paśyatīśa nikhilaṃ bhavadvapuḥ: he who sees this whole world-circle as Your body, without alternative.
Svātmapakṣaparipūrite jagaty asya nityasukhinaḥ kuto bhayam: in a world filled with self-nature, where is fear for the eternally happy?
The verse: seeing all as Your body, no fear for the eternally happy.
inference: Seeing all as Your body: no fear for the eternally happy in a world filled with self-nature.
uncertainties: Whether 'avikalpam' means 'without alternative' or 'without doubt' is unresolved.
Whether 'svātmapakṣa' means 'self-nature' or 'own side' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What becomes nectar?
premises: Kaṇṭhakoṇaviniviṣṭam īśa te kālakūṭam api me mahāmṛtam: the poison in the throat-corner, O Lord, is great nectar to me.
Apy upāttam amṛtaṃ bhavadvapur bhedavṛtti yadi rocate na me: even if Your body is nectar, division does not please me.
The verse: poison becomes nectar; division does not please.
inference: Poison becomes nectar to the devotee; division (bhedavṛtti) does not please.
uncertainties: Whether 'kaṇṭhakoṇa' means 'throat-corner' or 'corner of the throat' is unresolved.
Whether 'bhedavṛtti' means 'division' or 'differentiating activity' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What adorns?
premises: Tvadpralāpamayaraktagītikāni tya yuktavadanopaśobhitaḥ: adorned with speech full of Your prattle.
Syām athāpi bhavadarcanakriyāpreyasīparigatāśayaḥ sadā: may I be one whose mind is always intent on the beloved act of Your worship.
The verse: adorned with Your prattle, mind intent on worship.
inference: Adorned with Your prattle: may the mind be always intent on worship.
uncertainties: Whether 'pralāpamaya' means 'full of prattle' or 'full of Your speech' is unresolved.
Whether 'preyasīparigatāśaya' means 'mind intent on the beloved' or 'mind pervaded by love' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What can be counted?
premises: Īhitaṃ na bata pārameśvaraṃ śakyate gaṇayituṃ: the Lord's will cannot be counted.
Tathā ca me dattam apy amṛtanirbharaṃ vapuḥ svaṃ na pātum anumanyate tathā: even the nectar-filled body given to me is not allowed to be drunk.
The verse: the Lord's will is uncountable; even nectar given is not to be drunk.
inference: The Lord's will is uncountable; even nectar given is not to be drunk — the devotee does not consume.
uncertainties: Whether 'īhitaṃ' means 'will' or 'desire' is unresolved.
Whether 'anumanyate' means 'allowed' or 'permitted' is unresolved.

speaker: Utpaladeva (devotee's voice, first-person)
question: What is entered?
premises: Tvām agādham avikalpam advayaṃ svaṃ svarūpam akhilārthaghasmaram: You, unfathomable, without alternative, non-dual, own form, devourer of all things.
Āviśann aham umeśa sarvadā pūjayeyam abhisaṃstuvīya ca: entering, I will worship and praise always.
The verse: entering You, the unfathomable non-dual, worship and praise always.
inference: Entering You, the unfathomable non-dual — worship and praise always.
uncertainties: Whether 'agādham' means 'unfathomable' or 'bottomless' is unresolved.
Whether 'āviśann' means 'entering' or 'having entered' is unresolved.
